title: Ripple 65B Preview: Pricing, Speed, and Test Results
summary: Ripple 65B Preview assigns responsibility for automation errors to whoever implements it.
body_markdown:
## Ripple 65B Preview integration in workflows


To measure cost and speed you need the model inside a workflow. No dedicated connector for it was found as of 2026-11-08, so the route is generic building blocks, simplest first, with a named owner for each.


From least to most moving parts, the order is:


1. An HTTP request step that calls OpenRouter with the model` ricursiveai/ripple-65b-preview` .
2. An AI step pointed at a custom, OpenAI-compatible provider.
3. An MCP server, only if the model must call tools.


Stop at the first step that answers your test, because each one adds a component that someone must maintain.


### Option 1: an HTTP request step


Send a chat request to OpenRouter, a gateway that exposes many models behind one API and one key, with the model ID above, and the response carries the text you need.


Because you build the request yourself, you see exactly what was sent and returned, which makes timing and spend easy to log.


The cost is that retries and error handling are yours to write, and whoever owns the workflow gets paged when the call fails.


### Option 2: an AI step with a custom or OpenAI-compatible provider


If your workflow tool has a built-in AI step, point it at a custom provider using OpenRouter's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, your key, and the same model ID. Prompts then sit alongside your other AI steps, which is tidier.


The trade-off is that the step hides some of the raw request detail, so check that it exposes timing before you trust it for measurement.


When the model must act, such as querying a system, add Option 3, an MCP server. MCP, the Model Context Protocol, lets a model call external tools through a server. It brings a new service that someone has to host, secure and own.


[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) lets you put Ripple in that slot without the platform choosing a model for you: with your own provider key (Bring-Your-Own-Key, from the Plus plan up), model spend lands on your own provider bill at your own rates. Bring-your-own-key starts on the Plus plan at $20 a month, where every AI step counts as 1 credit whatever model sits behind it, so the model's price stays between you and OpenRouter. A platform that resells you its own model has made that decision and priced it before you open the product. Activepieces' MCP server reaches Claude, Cursor, Windsurf or any other MCP client, and the screenshot below shows its Client Setup Instructions:


- Tabs for Claude, Cursor, Windsurf and Server/Other
- A JSON block holding the endpoint


Take from it that the connection is a short configuration, and that the compatibility warning is the first thing to check before anyone commits time.
